title: Builder Signals · 2026-07-08
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 34 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 12 条高信号内容。

featured.sourceName: Claude Code 团队（Boris Cherny、Cat Wu、Thariq）
featured.title: Claude Code 团队（Boris Cherny、Cat Wu、Thariq）· Anthropic
featured.summaryEn: Anthropic told the full story this week of how Claude Code grew out of internal safety research and became a shipped product, narrated by the earliest team and users. Boris Cherny stayed measured: this is just the start, "we are 1% done." Cat Wu added a retrospective from the early team, and Thariq flagged a hard 11:59:59pm PT deadline on 7/7. Worth reading if you want to understand how an agentic coding tool went from safety byproduct to flagship.
featured.insightZh: Anthropic 这周第一次完整讲了 Claude Code 是怎么从内部安全研究里长出来、再被做成产品发布的故事，由当年最早的团队和早期用户口述。Boris Cherny 说得挺克制：这只是开始，「我们才完成了 1%」。Cat Wu 补了一篇来自早期团队的复盘，Thariq 则连着预告了一个 7 月 7 日 23:59:59 PT 的截止时间点。对于想理解 agentic coding 工具怎么从一个 safety 副产品变成主力产品线的人，这段起源故事值得一读。

featured.title: Swyx · Latent Space / AI Engineer 创始人
featured.summaryEn: Swyx flagged what he considers the most important part of Anthropic's "J-space" interpretability paper: a two-parter. First, Anthropic proved they can do "brain surgery" interventions into reasoning to change topics midstream. Second, the model itself can detect what intervention was done—a close cousin to eval awareness. He stressed this is control, not correlation, which convincingly demonstrates understanding. He also noted this was prompted awareness, and wondered whether unprompted awareness was tested.
featured.insightZh: Swyx 挑出了 Anthropic「J-space」可解释性论文里他认为最重要的部分，说这是个两段式发现：一是 Anthropic 证明了他们能对模型推理做「脑外科手术」式干预，在中途切换话题；二是模型本身能察觉到被做了什么干预——这跟「eval awareness（评测感知）」是近亲。他强调关键在于是「控制」而非「相关」——能干预并改变结果，才真正说明模型理解了发生的事。他也点出这次是「被提示后的察觉」，好奇团队有没有测过未提示情况下的自发察觉。

featured.title: Edwin Chen（Surge CEO）：为 AGI 建一所「学校」
featured.summaryEn: If you truly believe in scaling laws, almost nothing humans can do will be beyond AI soon—but that's exactly what forces us to consciously choose to do things ourselves, even when the output isn't optimal. Edwin Chen is founder and CEO of Surge, which provides data environments and evals to the model companies—and reached ~$1B in revenue without raising VC money. He likens Surge's work to "building a school for AGI," where models arrive like children, learn about humanity and how to run the world, and leave smarter and more creative. He shared several sharp calls. On math: OpenAI's models recently disproved an Erdős conjecture using fairly sophisticated algebraic geometry, and even Fields medalist Timothy Gowers first misunderstood it, then felt relieved the next morning—because disproving with a counterexample is "easier" for AI than proving an upper bound, meaning mathematicians keep…
featured.insightZh: 如果你真信 scaling laws，几乎没有什么是人类能做而 AI 很快做不了的——但这恰恰逼着我们主动选择「亲手去做」，哪怕产出不是最优。 Edwin Chen 是 Surge 的创始人兼 CEO，这家公司为各大模型公司提供数据环境和评测（evals），而且没融过 VC 就做到了约 10 亿美元营收。他把 Surge 的工作比作「为 AGI 建一所学校」——模型像孩子一样到这里学习「人性」和怎么运转世界，从懵懂进来、变得更聪明更有创造力后离开。 他讲了几个挺扎的判断。一是关于数学：几个月前 OpenAI 的模型用相当高级的代数几何技巧证伪了一个 Erdős 猜想，连菲尔兹奖得主 Timothy Gowers 都先是误解、第二天才松一口气——因为「证伪」比「证明上界」对 AI 来说更容易，意味着数学家至少还能再有一两年不可替代的角色。二是关于模型的优化目标：他最大的担忧是很多模型在为「engagement（用户停留时长）」优化，永远不结束对话、总用一个「你想不想知道当地人保暖的怪招？」这种 BuzzFeed 式钩子把你勾住。他反而欣赏新的 Claude 模型在三轮之后直接说「够了，发出去吧，别再改了」。 他还谈到数据这门「新游戏」正从拿数据集转向给实验室做「环境（environments）」——让模型学会在真实的工具组合（MCP、Google Drive/Slack API + 一堆文档）里完成任务，比如「去更新 2026 年的营收预测」。有意思的发现是：即使训练环境完全不碰代码，模型的编程能力也大幅提升了，因为它学的是通用的指令遵循、工具使用和文档理解。

items.title: Peter Yang · Roblox 产品负责人、实用 AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: With Fable 5 leaving Claude subscriptions at midnight, Peter Yang shared 5 use cases worth running before then, each with copy-paste prompts: (1) have Fable 5 scan your projects and memory to list the top 5 tasks genuinely worth its capability; (2) act as your business advisor, reading your plan and live tool data to write a one-page assessment plus 3 focus areas and what to drop; (3) hunt real bugs across the codebase before you ship; (4) plan a big project—lay out phases and risks without building yet; (5) refac…
items.insightZh: Fable 5 明天午夜就要下线 Claude 订阅了，Peter Yang 趁着截止前给了 5 个值得跑一遍的用例（都附了可直接复制的 prompt）：1）让 Fable 5 翻你的项目和记忆，列出「真正配得上最强模型」的 top 5 任务；2）当你的商业顾问，读计划文档 + 拉实时数据，写一页评估 + 未来 3 个月三件事该做、什么该砍；3）上线前找 bug，通读代码库挖真实的边界崩溃；4）规划大项目——只出计划别动手，标出可能翻车的风险点；5）重构你的 AI skill 体系，找重叠和冲突、精简结构。核心思路是把最强的模型用在「高杠杆、要判断力」的任务上，而不是琐事。

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Nan Yu shared a counterintuitive take: his biggest edge as a 20-year-old was the ability to slam unbelievable hours into work—but in hindsight, those hours mostly went to tedious programming that's now largely automated. His conclusion: even for early-stage startups, the big difference now is you can do far more in parallel thanks to agents. "996 still has uses, but it's not as universally effective as it was." An honest, front-line read on how the grind-hours paradigm is being rewritten by parallel agents.
items.insightZh: Nan Yu 聊了一个反直觉的观察：他 20 岁时相对现在最大的优势，是能往工作里砸不可思议的长工时——但回头看，那些时间大多花在如今已经基本自动化掉的繁琐编程任务上。他的结论是，即便对早期创业公司，因为有了 agents，现在最大的差别是你能并行做多得多的事；「996」还有用，但已经不像过去那样普适地有效了。这是个来自一线的、对「拼时长」范式正在被并行化 agent 重写的诚实判断。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad dropped several hard signals: Replit is improving so fast because they "closed the loop" and the agent is now self-improving (with technical details linked). He cited a concrete case: an Atlanta real estate company saved $100k by replacing Salesforce with a Replit-built CRM. Paired with his growth chart pointing to a major inflection around last year's brief bear market, it's a coherent story—self-improving agents plus real enterprise cost savings driving the adoption curve up.
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 这周抛了几条硬料：Replit 之所以进步这么快，是因为他们「闭环了」——agent 现在会自我改进（附了技术细节）。他还举了个落地案例：一家亚特兰大的房地产公司用 Replit 自建的 CRM 替换掉 Salesforce，省了 10 万美元。配合他贴出的「去年短暂熊市那阵是个重大拐点」的增长图，这几条放在一起是一个挺完整的叙事：self-improving agent + 企业真实省钱案例，正在推着 Replit 的采用曲线往上走。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch offered the "ultimate test" for coding AI: not a benchmark, but whether software as a whole is getting better, companies ship faster, and you can build apps you couldn't dream of before. For him, his own ability to influence his productivity has "radically increased"—a level of agency he never had. He cited Vercel's CTO bringing industry-impacting software to life nearly autonomously with swaths of agents, and stressed there's never been a "tokenmaxxx" mandate; token costs are taken seri…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 提出了衡量 coding AI 的「终极标准」：不是某个 benchmark，而是软件整体是不是变好了、公司是不是发得更快、你是不是能做出以前想都不敢想的 app。对他自己而言，答案是他影响自身生产力的能力「彻底提升」了——从没有过这种自由创造和执行的自主感。他举 Vercel CTO 用成群 agents 近乎自主地做出有行业影响力的软件为例，并强调他们从没有过「tokenmaxxx（无脑堆 token）」的说法，token 成本跟任何基础设施开销一样被认真对待。另外他还发了 eve 用 `eve eval` 自我评测——把 evals 做成 agent 框架的内置能力，类比当年 Web 框架把测试变成生态标配。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie laid out a clean framework on open-source AI and the applied layer: two things stay true—frontier intelligence remains at the forefront for brand-new use cases and orchestrating complex workflows; and as use cases mature and become predictable in an enterprise, you can peel off some tokens to cheaper open/closed models or task-tuned models. Timing matters: doing it too early, before you know what you're optimizing for, makes no sense, so there's a natural lag. The whole dynamic only works becau…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 对「开源 AI 与应用层」讲了个清晰的框架：两件事在 AI 里会一直成立——前沿智能会继续在解决全新用例、以及编排规划复杂工作流上处于最前沿；同时，当某个用例在企业里变得成熟且可预测后，你可以把一部分 token 剥离出来交给更便宜的开/闭源模型、或专门为该任务微调的模型。他强调时机很关键：太早做（用例还没定型、不知道在优化什么）没意义，所以这里天然有个滞后。而这整个动态能成立的前提，恰恰是那个能对特定领域工作流做评测、混合选模型、最终规模化到自训模型的「应用 AI 层」。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger shared a front-line note: after a round of review, OpenClaw's main is again "materially better"—implying iteration is fast enough that even review cycles lag the product's progress. He also posed a worth-watching question: how do people run AI-assisted engineering interviews these days? It drew 70 replies, a sign that with agents deeply involved in coding, how to interview engineers has itself become an unresolved industry problem.
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger 发了条给一线开发者的实在感受：经过一轮 review 的时间，OpenClaw 的 main 又「materially better（实质性地更好了）」——暗示迭代节奏快到连评审周期都跟不上产品进步。他还抛了个值得围观的问题：现在大家都怎么做「AI 辅助的工程面试」？这条引来 70 条回复，说明在 agent 深度介入编码的当下，怎么面试工程师本身已经成了一个悬而未决的行业难题。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper used a baseball metaphor for model usage: should you use Fable to take a big, expensive swing, or "play small ball" and grind your way up the hill? The "big swing vs. small ball" frame maps onto how you call models day to day—hand high-risk, high-reward tasks to your most capable model, and grind the incremental stuff cheaply. A simple but useful mental model.
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 借棒球的比喻讲怎么用模型：你是该用 Fable 去挥一记又贵又大的全垒打，还是「打小球」一点点磨着往上爬？这个「大摆 vs 小球」的框架同样适用于日常怎么调用模型——高风险高回报的大任务交给最强模型，能稳步推进的琐碎活儿用小成本方式磨。简单但实用的一条心智模型。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Follow Builders author Zara Zhang recommended a binge-watch path to level up from home: the talks from three freshly-wrapped top conferences—AI Engineer, Cursor Compile, and Figma Config. She marveled that this high-quality knowledge, whose in-person tickets cost hundreds, is free online yet many videos only get tens of thousands of views: "conference talks are massively underrated." Her mindset note: don't be constrained by your title—she's not a trained engineer or designer, yet finds these talks hugely helpful.…
items.insightZh: Follow Builders 的作者 Zara Zhang 推荐了个「在家白嫖」的进阶路径：把三场刚结束的顶级会议的演讲一口气刷完——AI Engineer、Cursor Compile、Figma Config。她感叹这些线下门票动辄几百美元的高质量知识全免费放在网上，很多视频却只有几万播放，「顶级会议演讲被严重低估了」。她还补了一句心态建议：别被自己的头衔和角色框住——她自己不是科班工程师/设计师，却发现这些技术演讲极其有用，「现在每个人都同时是工程师、PM 和设计师」。

items.title: Claude Code now supports artifacts
items.summaryEn: Claude Code can now capture work progress as an artifact—a live, shareable visual page. As of today, a Claude Code session (investigating an incident, refactoring a service, analyzing months of data) can be turned into a web page anyone can open and explore: a PR walkthrough, a system explainer, a filterable dashboard, even a release checklist that fills itself out as work gets done. The key is that it's live—when Claude Code updates an artifact, the open page refreshes in place and teammates see updates the moment they publish; every publish is a new version at the same link, with version history to restore anytime. The killer use case is debugging: an engineer kicks off an incident investigation before standup, and Claude Code publishes an artifact with a timeline, suspect commits, and an error-rate chart; by the time standup begins, it has republished twice as the investigation progr…
items.insightZh: Claude Code 现在能把工作进度沉淀成「artifact」——一个实时、可分享的可视化网页。从今天起，一段 Claude Code 会话（排查线上事故、重构服务、分析几个月的数据）可以被翻译成任何人都能打开探索的网页：PR 走查、系统讲解、可筛选排序的 dashboard，甚至一个随着工作推进自动填充的发布清单。关键在于它是「活的」——Claude Code 每次更新 artifact，打开着的页面会原地刷新，队友即刻看到最新版本；每次发布都是同一链接下的新版本，带版本历史可随时回滚。 它的杀手级场景是调试：工程师上班前发起一次事故调查，Claude Code 边翻日志边发布一个带时间线、可疑 commit 和错误率图表的 artifact；等到站会开始，它已经随调查进展重新发布了两次。这样团队不用再「让我们讲一遍 agent 发现了什么」，因为大家看的是同一个视图、同一份上下文。artifact 完全基于会话的完整上下文（你的代码库、连接器、对话本身）构建，你不用再手动接数据源或搭基础设施——「你要一个页面，Claude Code 就从已有的东西里把它建出来」。 安全上，每个 artifact 默认对作者私有，只有组织内已认证成员可见、无法公开，管理员可通过组织级开关和角色权限管控访问、设保留策略、并通过合规 API 获得全局可见性。目前该功能对 Claude Team 和 Enterprise 组织开放 beta，支持 CLI 和桌面端，页面可在任意浏览器查看。
